content: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 150, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, happy Halloween, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.) This week, I was in the Smoky Mountains in Tennessee on a family vacation. It was delightful (and the reason this week’s Installer is a little short). I’ve also been reading about job hunting and 30 Rock and crypto detectives, testing the DuckDuckGo browser after a bunch of you told me to add it to the list, watching the adorable new Pixar short over and over, getting caught up on VisionQuest, playing with my new Pebble Index 01 now that it finally arrived, listening to music on my rad-looking new CMF Speaker S, and eating a worrying number of pumpkin chocolate chip muffins. I also have for you some new gear from Apple and Amazon, a better way to read books on your phone, a resurrected note-taking app, an absurdly expensive robovac, and much more. Let’s do it. (As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you watching / reading / listening to / playing / giving to trick-or-treaters this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.) The Drop * The new iPad Mini. With apologies to the touchscreen MacBook, this is the most intriguing new Apple product of the week. I, too, am annoyed that there’s no ProMotion screen, but I’m excited about thinner and lighter, and I’m very excited about the idea of a functionally water- and dustproof tablet. * The Alexa Photo Frame. The Echo Show 16 is a cool smart home hub, but $500 is just too much for me. But a $200 digital photo frame that is also, sometimes, only when you need it, a smart home hub and timer-setter? That will end up in my living room. And my parents’. And my in-laws’. * nvAlt. One of the all-time great note-taking apps got its first update in forever, and now it can run on modern Macs. (The developer is also working on nvUltra, which is in beta and even better.) If you’re a plain-text notetaker, you’re gonna want to get back into this app. * Chromagraph. The director Rian Johnson — yes, that one — worked with his favorite cinematographer to make it possible to process iPhone photos the way they like best. An extremely opinionated camera app from people who have very much earned those opinions. I love it. * “I love the iPod. It ruined everything.” This Mic The Snare video is both a very good history of the iPod and a surprisingly cogent theory that the iPod is to blame for some of the worst things about modern life. I still miss my gold iPod Mini. * Readwise Books. A really nice-looking, really powerful app for buying, reading, and tracking your books. Right now it’s a little bit “better Kindle” and a lot “better Goodreads.” So far I’m mostly using the social feed to get recommendations from strangers, which suits me just fine. This went right onto my Boox Palma homescreen. * Phantom Blade Zero. Currently burning up the Steam charts, this one. People love the martial arts-inspired combat system and the game’s overall aesthetic, and I’m even hearing good things about the music. * No Man’s Sky. This is definitely one of the biggest and most ambitious games to ever come to iOS (and all it took was a decade!). It works on pretty much all recent iPhones and iPads, too. Just don’t be fooled by the Free sign at the top; the game costs $20. But it’s worth it. * The Matic Serene. Two things here. One, $1,700 is an absolutely ludicrous price for a robot vacuum, no matter how good it is. Two, “we made it quieter” is maybe the quickest way to get me in particular to want your robot vacuum. Please, friends, do not let me buy this. Crowdsourced Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky. “Currently watching: VisionQuest. It’s quite good! James Spader has really stolen the show, but I am a little biased as a huge Blacklist fan.” — Spencer “I’m using CallMe to coordinate when my friends and I call each other. You can tap ‘I’m free for the next 15/30/60 minutes’ and your friends will get a notification. When you’re both free you can call each other (outside of the app). Makes it easy to reconnect.” — Jordan “I’ve been spending the last few days working on my Top 10 for WXPN’s annual Top 885. This year is ‘Top 885 Songs from Movies and TV,’ and it’s especially challenging.” — Ben “The one game that I play religiously is Clues By Sam, a daily logic puzzle game where speed and accuracy is the goal. Because everyone starts at the same spot, your time is your score, and it’s very fun competing with friends every day. Puzzles range from easy (~2 minutes) on Mondays to Brutal (up to ~15 minutes) on Sundays. Would 100% recommend adding it to your daily rotation.” — Adam “Maybe niche, but Steam Frame and trying out older 3D media on it that flopped or became obsolete. Stereoscopic 3DS games and 3D movies work better than they ever did on original hardware, on devices with a dedicated individual display for each eye.” — Mango “I am sooo into the Vivaldi browser now, with the look and feel, and all the customisations! 😍” — Oscar “Spending some more time learning about the AT Protocol for a class project. The tech is neat. Fell down the rabbit hole of mental poker cryptography.” — James “The YouTube channel Digging the Greats by Brandon Shaw is fantastic for music lovers like myself. chineseContent: 嗨，朋友们！欢迎来到《Installer No. 150》，这是您了解世界上最好、最前沿的东西的指南。 （如果您是新来的，欢迎光临，万圣节快乐，您也可以在安装程序主页上阅读所有旧版本。） 本周，我在田纳西州的大烟山与家人一起度假。这很令人愉快（这也是本周安装程序有点短的原因）。我还阅读了关于找工作和 30 名摇滚和密码侦探的文章，在一群人告诉我将其添加到列表中后测试了 DuckDuckGo 浏览器，一遍又一遍地观看可爱的新皮克斯短片，关注 VisionQuest，玩我的新 Pebble Index 01（现在它终于到了），在我看起来很酷的新 CMF 扬声器 S 上听音乐，并吃了数量令人担忧的南瓜巧克力片松饼。我还为您准备了一些来自苹果和亚马逊的新设备、一种在手机上读书的更好方式、一款复活的笔记应用程序、一款贵得离谱的 robovac 等等。我们开始做吧。 （与往常一样，Installer 的最佳部分是您的想法和提示。本周您正在看/读/听/玩/给“不给糖就捣蛋”的人什么？请告诉我一切：installer@theverge.com。如果您认识其他可能喜欢 Installer 的人，请将其转发给他们并告诉他们在此处订阅。） The Drop * 新 iPad Mini。向触摸屏 MacBook 致歉，这是本周最吸引人的苹果新产品。我也对没有 ProMotion 屏幕感到恼火，但我对更薄、更轻感到兴奋，而且我对功能性防水和防尘平板电脑的想法感到非常兴奋。 * Alexa 相框。 Echo Show 16 是一款很酷的智能家居中心，但 500 美元对我来说太贵了。但是，一个 200 美元的数码相框，有时，只有当你需要它时，它才是一个小东西。
